text:
Alex Chen: quick sync — noticed some hosted streaming requests that retried mid-stream are getting billed twice for overlapping tokens. example: client sees partial output A, retries, gets B, and billing shows both A and B charged. we need a way to checkpoint consumption so retries can be reconciled. @Maria any ideas? :thinking:
Maria Gomez: Yea I've seen this. root cause is we count tokens at the edge as soon as they're emitted. if we can't distinguish 'committed' progress vs 'speculative' mid-stream, replays double-count. proposal: emit immutable 'checkpoint-id' trailer when chunk is durable. edge persists checkpoint -> billing only counts checkpointed progress. until checkpoint, charge as 'pending' and reconcile on commit.
Dave Patel: compatibility concerns: many clients/proxies won't forward trailers, and gRPC streams behave differently. Also what about short-lived connections where client disconnects before commit? Who owns commit TTL?
Sylvia Ho: idea: use a header-forwarded GUID and per-chunk progress markers in-band. e.g.

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
X-Stream-Checkpoint: 1693600000-<uuid>-offset=1024
{ "delta": "hello" }
```

Edge would store latest checkpoint per request-id. Billing job tallies checkpoints periodically. If retry happens with same request-id, we reconcile by comparing checkpoint offsets. Could work across protocols if we normalize markers.
Alex Chen: that helps. but two gotchas: 1) side-effectful ops (webhooks, DB writes) — we must not replay side effects. 2) rate-limiter/quota: pending tokens shouldn't be spendable by other flows. any thoughts?
Maria Gomez: For side-effects we should enforce 'at-most-once' via idempotency keys. If request has side-effects, client must pass Idempotency-Key and we treat checkpoint commit as the point-of-no-return. For rate-limiting: track 'reserved' token counts for pending progress on a per-tenant basis; release on explicit commit or TTL expiry. This avoids artificially hoarding.
Dave Patel: Implementation sketch: edge assigns request-id and tentative-offsets. Upstream returns checksums for chunks optionally. Billing service subscribes to checkpoint events (pubsub). Reconciliation worker aggregates checkpoints and emits final invoiceable deltas. Fallback: if client disconnects w/o commit, after N seconds roll forward best-effort commit or mark as abandoned and bill only last committed checkpoint.
Sylvia Ho: what about privacy & logs? storing partial outputs might be sensitive. store minimal metadata (offsets, checksums, sizes) not full tokens unless customer opts in.
Alex Chen: agree. ops concerns: storage churn for many short lived streams. propose S3-like TTL buckets for checkpoints, compacted every hour.
Maria Gomez: next steps: prototype header-based checkpoint markers + billing consumer. I'll spin up a small PoC in eng-runtime sandbox. @Sylvia want to pair on the privacy packing? :+1:
Sylvia Ho: yes. I'll add a design doc stub with compatibility matrix (HTTP/2, SSE, gRPC, websockets) and list of header bindings.
ingress-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T14:12:03Z: feature/edge-checkpoint-proto rolled to canary (20%). watch logs in #eng-runtime.
Alex Chen: thanks team — capture action items and sync in design review Wed 10am. I'll add to agenda.
